the potential of Wnt/ß-catenin inhibitors to enhance the elimination of prostate cancer cells by lymphocytes from patients.
the development of a novel immunotherapeutic approach to treat patients with BRPCa.

XAV939 enhances cancer cell elimination by BRPCa patient lymphocytes in the in vitro coculture system, but that this enhancement is only temporary.
the Wnt/ β-catenin signaling inhibitors may be useful for enhancing cell-based immunotherapy in prostate cancer.
the Wnt/ β-catenin signaling inhibitors XAV939 and ICG-001 can be combined with cell-based immunotherapy for PCa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Wnt/β- catenin signaling inhibition in cancer cells can enhance the elimination of cancer cells by patient lymphocytes, but Wnt/β-catenn signaling inhibition in patient lymphocytes is required to prevent the development of cancer cell-eliciting immunosuppression.
Wnt/β- catenin signaling inhibitors can be used to enhance the efficacy of cancer cell-elimination by immune cells, but the benefit(s) are likely to be short-lived.
the inhibition of Wnt/ β-catenin signaling in PCa cells and PCa lymphocytes enhances the elimination of PCa cells by PCa lymphocytes in vitro.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Wnt/ β-catenin signaling pathway can be a target to enhance cancer immunotherapeutic strategies.
the therapeutic benefit of inhibitors of Wnt signaling is dependent on the cancer cell type and the cancer cell line.
the therapeutic impact of inhibitors of Wnt signaling will depend on the status of Wnt signaling in both the target cancer cells and the immune cells.
